title: Sky retains the majority of each Prime's token supply and spends it acquiring USDS users
content:
A.2.8.2.2.2.1.1 fixes both SPK and GROVE supply at ten billion. A.2.8.2.2.2.1.2.1 allocates three billion GROVE to the Grove Foundation, and A.2.8.2.2.2.1.2.2 states that "Sky retains 7,000,000,000 GROVE tokens and 6,500,000,000 SPK tokens," distributed "as token rewards over time as determined by Sky Governance."

The majority of a Prime's token supply therefore sits with Sky, not with the Prime. That inverts the usual relationship between a protocol and its token: the Prime issues the token, but Sky holds and directs most of it.

The schedules in A.2.8.2.2.2.1.2.2.1 and .2 show what it is for. About 4.9bn GROVE and 4.55bn SPK go "to USDS users" over ten years, front-loaded and stepping down repeatedly — 1.225bn GROVE in each of years one and two, halving to 612.5m, then 306.25m, then 153.125m for the final four years. SPK follows the identical shape at a slightly lower level.

Read as a whole, Prime tokens function as a **user-acquisition currency for USDS**. A Prime's equity subsidises demand for Sky's stablecoin, with the heaviest incentives during the years when adoption is being established and a long tail afterwards to avoid a cliff.

What remains with Sky beyond the schedules — roughly 2.1bn GROVE and 1.95bn SPK — is "reserved for future token rewards as determined by Sky Governance," an undesignated reserve at governance's discretion. The arrangement gives Sky both the incentive budget and the residual, which is a substantial claim on the value a Prime creates and is worth reading alongside the recourse provisions that also run through these tokens.
description: Of ten billion tokens each, Sky holds 7bn GROVE and 6.5bn SPK, distributing roughly 4.9bn and 4.55bn to USDS users over ten years on a front-loaded, repeatedly halving schedule.
